This creamy, flavorful soup is incredibly easy to make, offering a hearty and nourishing meal that warms the soul. Perfect for any time of year, it embodies the rich, simple goodness of traditional Turkish cuisine.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. Set aside to drain. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Sauté Garlic and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste, cooking it for 1-2 minutes to deepen its flavor and color, stirring constantly to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the dried mint and sweet paprika, cooking for about 30 seconds until aromatic. Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring well to coat them with the spice and aromatic mixture.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the hot water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend and Season
instructions.text: Carefully remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until desired consistency is reached.

instructions.title: Prepare the Topping and Serve
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the red pepper flakes (pul biber) and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant and vibrant in color. Be careful not to burn the butter. Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving with a spoonful of the spiced butter and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges for squeezing.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, toast the dried mint and paprika briefly in the pot before adding liquids. This brings out their essential oils and deepens the aroma.
Always rinse your red lentils thoroughly to remove any impurities and excess starch, which helps achieve a clearer, smoother soup texture. Do not skip this step.
Adjust the consistency of your soup after blending. If you prefer a thinner soup, gradually add more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired texture. Taste and re-season as needed.
article:
Embrace the warmth and comfort of a culinary journey to Turkey with Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, wholesome, and incredibly flavorful soup is a cornerstone of Turkish cuisine, gracing tables from bustling street-side eateries to elegant family dinners. Its rich, earthy notes, combined with a subtle tang and a hint of spice, make it an irresistible choice for any meal. Whether you're seeking a nourishing starter or a light yet satisfying main course, Mercimek Corbasi delivers a comforting embrace in every spoonful.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi (pronounced mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-SUH) is a quintessential Turkish soup, renowned for its beautiful reddish-orange hue and velvety smooth texture. At its heart, it’s a simple yet profoundly satisfying dish made primarily from red lentils, aromatics like onion and garlic, and a blend of traditional Turkish spices. Unlike some lentil soups that maintain the whole lentil shape, Mercimek Corbasi is typically pureed to a creamy consistency, making it wonderfully comforting and easy to digest.

This soup is more than just food; it’s a symbol of Turkish hospitality and home cooking. It’s often the first course offered, a warm welcome that prepares the palate for the feast to come. Its origins are humble, rooted in the resourcefulness of Anatolian cooking, where lentils were a readily available and nutritious staple. Today, it remains a testament to the fact that the most delicious dishes often come from the simplest ingredients, transformed by time-honored techniques and a touch of culinary magic. The unique flavor profile, often brightened by a squeeze of fresh lemon and sometimes finished with a drizzle of chili-infused mint butter, sets Turkish Red Lentil Soup apart from other lentil preparations around the world.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its straightforward ingredient list, where each component plays a crucial role in building its distinctive flavor. To make an authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup, you'll need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. These quick-cooking legumes break down beautifully, contributing to the soup's signature creamy texture. Ensure they are well-rinsed.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. Sautéed until fragrant, they provide depth and a savory base.
*   **Tomato Paste:** Adds a rich umami flavor and contributes to the soup's characteristic reddish color.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** For sautéing the aromatics and building flavor.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** A non-negotiable ingredient in Turkish cuisine, dried mint offers a unique freshness and aromatic complexity that defines this soup.
*   **Pul Biber (Aleppo Pepper Flakes) or Paprika:** For a gentle warmth and vibrant color. Pul biber offers a mild, fruity heat.
*   **Cumin:** Earthy and warm, cumin complements the lentils beautifully, adding an essential layer of flavor.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** The liquid base for cooking the lentils. Broth will add more depth.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season and enhance all the flavors.
*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** Crucial for serving, a squeeze of lemon brightens the entire soup.

Optional additions for serving include fresh mint leaves, extra pul biber, or a drizzle of "nane yagi" (melted butter infused with dried mint and chili flakes).

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Mercimek Corbasi

Creating a delicious Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a rewarding process, and these steps will guide you to a perfect bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Begin by thoroughly rinsing 1 cup (about 200g) of red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This helps remove any impurities and starch, preventing the soup from becoming cloudy. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 2-3 cloves of minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Build the Flavor Base:** Stir in 1 tablespoon of tomato paste, 1 teaspoon of dried mint, 1 teaspoon of cumin, and 1/2 to 1 teaspoon of pul biber (or paprika, to taste). Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing the spices and tomato paste to toast and deepen in flavor. This step is crucial for unlocking the full aroma.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in 6-7 cups (1.5-1.75 liters) of water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely soft and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend to Perfection:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be very cautious with hot liquids and vent the lid) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
6.  **Season and Adjust Consistency:** Return the soup to low heat. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick for your preference, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Let it simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
7.  **Optional Mint Butter Drizzle (Nane Yagi):** In a small pan, melt 1-2 tablespoons of butter over low heat. Add 1/2 teaspoon of pul biber and 1/2 teaspoon of dried mint. Cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices. This vibrant oil is drizzled over individual servings.

## Pro Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that perfect, comforting bowl of Mercimek Corbasi involves a few insider tricks that elevate it from good to unforgettable.

*   **Rinse Those Lentils Thoroughly:** This isn't just about cleanliness; it's about texture. Rinsing red lentils removes excess starch, which can make your soup cloudy or gummy. A good rinse ensures a clear, vibrant color and a smoother finish.
*   **Don't Rush the Aromatics:** Sautéing the onions until deeply translucent and the garlic until fragrant is key to building a robust flavor base. Similarly, cooking the tomato paste and spices for a minute or two before adding liquid allows their flavors to bloom and intensify, adding depth to your Turkish Red Lentil Soup.
*   **The Power of Dried Mint:** While fresh mint is wonderful, dried mint (nane) has a unique, concentrated flavor that is absolutely essential for authentic Mercimek Corbasi. Don't skip it, and consider adding it both during cooking and in the optional butter drizzle.
*   **Blend Until Velvety Smooth:** The signature texture of this soup is its creaminess. Use an immersion blender or a regular blender to achieve a perfectly smooth consistency, free of any lentil chunks. This makes it incredibly comforting and appealing.
*   **Lemon is Non-Negotiable:** A fresh squeeze of lemon juice stirred into the soup just before serving, or offered at the table, is transformative. It cuts through the richness, brightens all the flavors, and adds a crucial tangy note that balances the earthiness of the lentils.
*   **Consider the Nane Yagi:** While optional, the chili-mint butter drizzle (nane yagi) is a traditional flourish that adds a beautiful visual appeal, a layer of rich flavor, and a subtle warmth. It's an easy way to make your soup feel even more special and authentic.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. It’s often served as a hearty starter, but paired with the right accompaniments, it makes for a satisfying light meal.

*   **Garnishes:** A simple drizzle of the optional nane yagi (chili-mint butter) is traditional and highly recommended. Other popular garnishes include a sprinkle of fresh chopped mint or parsley, a pinch of pul biber for an extra kick, or a swirl of plain yogurt for a cooling contrast.
*   **Bread is Essential:** No Turkish soup is complete without bread for dipping. Crusty Turkish bread (ekmek), a soft pita, or even a simple crusty baguette are perfect for soaking up every last drop of the delicious broth.
*   **Pickles & Salad:** A side of Turkish pickles (tursu) or a simple shepherd's salad (çoban salatası) with tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions, provides a refreshing counterpoint to the warmth of the soup.
*   **Mezze Platter:** For a more elaborate meal, serve Mercimek Corbasi as part of a mezze (appetizer) platter alongside hummus, babaganoush, olives, and other small dishes.
*   **As a Light Meal:** Enjoy a large bowl of Turkish Red Lentil Soup with a generous squeeze of lemon and a side of fresh bread for a wholesome and comforting lunch or dinner.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences without losing its essence.

*   **Vegan/Vegetarian:** Mercimek Corbasi is naturally vegan and vegetarian if you use olive oil instead of butter and vegetable broth instead of water. No other substitutions are typically needed.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of pul biber or paprika to your liking. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper. For a milder soup, reduce or omit the chili flakes.
*   **Adding Vegetables:** While traditionally a smooth, pureed soup, you can add finely diced carrots, potatoes, or bell peppers along with the lentils for extra nutrients and texture. These will also be blended smooth.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are traditional for their quick cooking and ability to break down, you could experiment with yellow lentils, though they might yield a slightly different texture and color.
*   **Smoked Paprika:** For a deeper, smokier flavor profile, substitute regular paprika with smoked paprika. This adds another layer of complexity.
*   **Gluten-Free:** This soup is naturally gluten-free, making it a great option for those with gluten sensitivities. Just ensure your broth is also gluten-free.
*   **Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional, a small amount of fresh parsley or cilantro can be added at the end for an extra burst of freshness, though this deviates slightly from the classic profile.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Mercimek Corbasi healthy?**
Absolutely! Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly healthy. Red lentils are a powerhouse of nutrition, rich in plant-based protein, dietary fiber, iron, and various B vitamins. The soup is low in fat, and when made with olive oil and vegetable broth, it's a fantastic choice for a balanced diet.

**Can I make Turkish Red Lentil Soup ahead of time?**
Yes, Mercimek Corbasi is an excellent make-ahead dish. In fact, many people find that its flavors deepen and improve after a day or two in the refrigerator. It reheats beautifully on the stovetop over low heat, adding a little extra water or broth if it has thickened too much.

**Can I freeze Mercimek Corbasi?**
Mercimek Corbasi freezes exceptionally well. Allow the soup to cool completely, then transfer it to airtight, freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop, adjusting consistency with a splash of water or broth if needed.

**What's the difference between red and yellow lentil soup?**
While both are delicious, red lentils (like those used in Mercimek Corbasi) tend to break down more completely when cooked, resulting in a smoother, creamier soup. Yellow lentils often hold their shape a bit more, leading to a slightly chunkier texture, and they have a milder, sweeter flavor profile compared to red lentils.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's a comforting hug in a bowl, a taste of Turkish tradition that transcends borders. Its simple ingredients, vibrant flavors, and nourishing qualities make it a perfect addition to any kitchen. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the timeless appeal of this exquisite Turkish Red Lentil Soup. Afiyet olsun (bon appétit)!
